D000163.s: An acquired defect of cellular immunity associated with infection by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), a CD4-positive T-lymphocyte count under 200 cells/microliter or less than 14% of total lymphocytes, and increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections and malignant neoplasms.

D000291.s: Diseases of the uterine appendages (adnexa uteri) including diseases involving the ovary, the fallopian tubes, and ligaments of the uterus (broad ligament; round ligament).

D000435.s: An acute brain syndrome which results from the excessive ingestion of ethanol or alcoholic beverages.

D000686.s: A group of sporadic, familial and/or inherited, degenerative, and infectious disease processes, linked by the common theme of abnormal protein folding and deposition of amyloid. As the amyloid deposits enlarge they displace normal tissue structures, causing disruption of function.

D000800.s: Use of a balloon catheter for dilation of an occluded artery. It is used in treatment of arterial occlusive diseases, including renal artery stenosis and arterial occlusions in the leg. For the specific technique of balloon dilation in coronary arteries, angioplasty, balloon, coronary is available.

D001766.s: The inability to see or the loss or absence of perception of visual stimuli. This condition may be the result of eye diseases; optic nerve diseases; optic chiasm diseases; or brain diseases affecting the visual pathways or occipital lobe.

D003337.s: Broad plate of dense myelinated fibers that reciprocally interconnect regions of the cortex in all lobes with corresponding regions of the opposite hemisphere. The corpus callosum is located deep in the longitudinal fissure.

D004637.s: Organized services to provide immediate psychiatric care to patients with acute psychological disturbances.

D004916.s: A peripheral arterial disease that is characterized by the triad of erythema, burning PAIN, and increased skin temperature of the extremities (or red, painful extremities). Erythromelalgia may be classified as primary or idiopathic, familial or non-familial.

D005506.s: The presence in food of harmful, unpalatable, or otherwise objectionable foreign substances, e.g. chemicals, microorganisms or diluents, before, during, or after processing or storage.

D005920.s: The thin membranous structure supporting the adjoining glomerular capillaries. It is composed of glomerular mesangial cells and their extracellular matrix.

D006349.s: Pathological conditions involving any of the various heart valves and the associated structures (papillary muscles and chordae tendineae).

D006558.s: Infection of the genitals (genitalia) with herpes simplex virus in either the males or the females.

D006644.s: Macrophages found in the tissues, as opposed to those found in the blood (monocytes) or serous cavities (serous membrane).

D007746.s: The position or orientation of the fetus at near term or during obstetric labor, determined by its relation to the spine of the mother and the birth canal. The normal position is a vertical, cephalic presentation with the fetal vertex flexed on the NECK.

D008066.s: The metabolic process of breaking down lipids to release free fatty acids, the major oxidative fuel for the body. Lipolysis may involve dietary lipids in the digestive tract, circulating lipids in the blood, and stored lipids in the adipose tissue or the liver.

D009887.s: Examination of the interior of the eye with an ophthalmoscope.

D010175.s: WHO regional office for the Americas acting as a coordinating agency for the improvement of health conditions in the hemisphere. The four main functions are: control or eradication of communicable diseases, strengthening of national and local health services, education and training, and research.

D010373.s: Parasitic attack or subsistence on the skin by members of the order Phthiraptera, especially on humans by Pediculus humanus of the family Pediculidae. The hair of the head, eyelashes, and pubis is a frequent site of infestation. (From Dorland, 28th ed; Stedman, 26th ed)

D010874.s: An infectious disease of the skin caused by Treponema carateum that occurs only in the western hemisphere. Age of onset is between 10 and 20 years of age. This condition is characterized by marked changes in the skin color and is believed to be transmitted by direct person-to-person contact.

D011200.s: Domesticated birds raised for food. It typically includes chickens; turkeys, ducks; geese; and others.

D011891.s: Water particles that fall from the atmosphere.

D013347.s: Components of a cell produced by various separation techniques which, though they disrupt the delicate anatomy of a cell, preserve the structure and physiology of its functioning constituents for biochemical and ultrastructural analysis.

D013732.s: A self-reporting test consisting of items concerning fear and worry about taking tests and physiological activity, such as heart rate, sweating, etc., before, during, and after tests.

D013897.s: The largest lymphatic vessel that passes through the chest and drains into the subclavian vein.

D014221.s: A glucocorticoid given, as the free alcohol or in esterified form, orally, intramuscularly, by local injection, by inhalation, or applied topically in the management of various disorders in which corticosteroids are indicated. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p739)

D014438.s: The classic form of typhus, caused by rickettsia prowazekii, which is transmitted from man to man by the louse Pediculus humanus corporis.

D014672.s: Recording of the moment-to-moment electromotive forces of the heart on a plane of the body surface delineated as a vector function of time.

D014904.s: A state in western Australia. Its capital is Perth. It was first visited by the Dutch in 1616 but the English took possession in 1791 and permanent colonization began in 1829.

D015279.s: Beliefs and values shared by all members of the organization. These shared values, which are subject to change, are reflected in the day to day management of the organization.

e: Congenital Icthyosis Mental Retardation Spasticity Syndrome
Ichthyosis, Spastic Neurologic Disorder, and Oligophrenia
D016111.s: An autosomal recessive neurocutaneous disorder characterized by severe ichthyosis mental retardation; spastic paraplegia; and congenital ichthyosis. It is caused by mutation of gene encoding microsomal fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase leading to defect in fatty alcohol metabolism.

D016429.s: Work that consists of a conference of physicians on their observations of a patient at the bedside, regarding the physical state, laboratory and other diagnostic findings, clinical manifestations, results of current therapy, etc.

D016678.s: The genetic complement of an organism, including all of its genes, as represented in its DNA, or in some cases, its RNA.

e: Ulnar Nerve Entrapment at the Wrist
D017769.s: Ulnar neuropathies caused by mechanical compression of the nerve at any location from its origin at the brachial plexus to its terminations in the hand.

e: Rutledge Lethal Multiple Congenital Anomaly Syndrome
D019082.s: An autosomal recessive disorder of cholesterol metabolism. It is caused by a deficiency of 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase, the enzyme that converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol, leading to an abnormally low plasma cholesterol.

D019424.s: An island republic of the West Indies. Its capital is Roseau. It was discovered in 1493 by Columbus and held at different times by the French and the British in the 18th century. A member of the West Indies Federation, it achieved internal self-government in 1967 but became independent in 1978.

D019873.s: An extremely rare condition manifested as monoclonal immunoglobulin M dysproteinemia without features of lymphoproliferative disease, but with chronic urticaria, fever of unknown origin, disabling bone pain, hyperostosis, and increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate.

D019969.s: Disorders related or resulting from use of amphetamines.

D022202.s: DNA constructs that are composed of, at least, a replication origin, for successful replication, propagation to and maintenance as an extra chromosome in bacteria. In addition, they can carry large amounts (about 200 kilobases) of other sequence for a variety of bioengineering purposes.

D032342.s: Mature contractile cells, commonly known as myocytes, that form one of three kinds of muscle. The three types of muscle cells are skeletal (muscle fibers, skeletal), cardiac (myocytes, cardiac), and smooth (myocytes, smooth muscle).

D038524.s: A diagnostic technique that incorporates the measurement of molecular diffusion (such as water or metabolites) for tissue assessment by MRI. The degree of molecular movement can be measured by changes of apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) with time, as reflected by tissue microstructure.

D039563.s: A class of non-sedating drugs that bind to but do not activate histamine receptors (drug inverse agonism), thereby blocking the actions of histamine or histamine agonists.

D051271.s: Conditions with headache symptom that can be attributed to a variety of causes including brain vascular disorders; wounds and injuries; infection; drug use or its withdrawal.

D051639.s: Cultivation of plants; (fruit; vegetables; medicinal herbs) on small plots of ground or in containers.

D054526.s: The concept covering the physical and mental conditions of men.

D056865.s: Expected weight of a healthy normal individual based on age, sex, and height. Thus, a malnourished person would weigh less than their ideal body weight.

D058427.s: Materials that readily absorb moisture from their surroundings.

D059370.s: The processes of RNA tertiary structure formation.

e: Transfer from Pediatric to Adult Care
D060305.s: Transfer from pediatric to adult care.

D061221.s: Traumatic injuries to the trigeminal nerve. It may result in extreme pain, abnormal sensation in the areas the nerve innervates on face, jaw, gums and tongue and can cause difficulties with speech and chewing. It is sometimes associated with various dental treatments.

D064891.s: Persons adversely effected by disasters, occurrences that result in property damage, deaths, and/or injuries to a community.

e: Anodal Stimulation Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
Cathodal Stimulation Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
D065908.s: A technique of brain electric stimulation therapy which uses constant, low current delivered via electrodes placed on various locations on the scalp.

e: Men Who Have Sex With Men
Women Who Have Sex With Women

D000075529.s: Either a single or a single functioning kidney due to nephrectomy, birth defects or other kidney diseases.

D000080925.s: Use of microwaves as a diagnostic tool.

D000089944.s: A posture in which an ideal body mass distribution is achieved for the abdominal core. Abdominal core stability and balance provides the body an ability to maintain equilibrium and control of the spine and pelvic region during movement.

D000092005.s: Hypoglycemic agents that stimulate insulin secretion from the pancreatic beta cell to decrease postprandial blood glucose.

e: Dynamic Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction
D000092243.s: Occlusion of the outflow tract in the right ventricle of the heart.

D000098542.s: A disease in which serum antibodies are directed against myelin-oligodendrocyte glycoprotein. Mogad is typically associated with acute disseminated encephalomyelitis; neuromyelitis optica; or transverse myelitis.
